patterns_proposed.rule_text: When a head-noun phrase in object-position or qualifier-clause is immediately followed by a parenthetical containing coordinated-clause noun phrases, extract each parenthetical noun phrase as a standalone candidate if the main predicate assigns placement, containment, or location to the outer phrase. Treat each extracted parenthetical noun phrase as linked by alias-defined-parenthetically or sub-element-of to the outer phrase, and preserve both exact-match and partial-match forms. Do not extract from a parenthetical whose content lacks noun-phrase structure or functions only as adverbial explanation.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: "The items are placed in a reserved area (a remote unit and a local unit) before later processing." -> extract separate candidates for both parenthetical noun phrases.
FP: "The items are placed in a reserved area (for stability and for speed) before later processing." -> do not extract candidates from the parenthetical.
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: The rule depends only on parenthetical structure, coordinated noun-phrase form, and predicate scope. It does not rely on any domain lexicon or architecture-specific naming convention, so it applies wherever documentation introduces an outer phrase and then enumerates internal alternatives or aliases in parentheses.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: in each case, documentation can use the same parenthetical coordinated noun-phrase pattern after a location or containment predicate, independent of component type. The trigger is syntactic: head-noun + parenthetical + coordinated noun phrases under one predicate. No style-specific role noun is required. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: Do not down-rank a candidate solely because the sentence-position begins with a contrastive or concessive discourse marker. Judge mention validity from the main predicate and its argument structure: if the sentence still asserts placement, containment, or location for a noun phrase, preserve the candidate. Reject only when the sentence contains discourse contrast without a noun-phrase candidate governed by such a predicate.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: "However, the attachments remain in a separate area for later access." -> keep the area mention valid.
FP: "However, the earlier claim was inaccurate." -> do not approve any candidate from the discourse marker alone.
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: This rule separates discourse function from entity evidence. Contrastive openers occur across documentation styles, but they do not alter whether a later predicate introduces a valid mention; the decision remains grounded in syntax and predicate-argument structure.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: all can contain sentence-initial contrast markers in explanatory prose, and in all five the marker is orthogonal to whether a later noun phrase is licensed by a placement or containment predicate. The rule uses only discourse-marker position and predicate structure, not style-specific semantics. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: Allow one sentence to validate multiple links when a single predicate scopes over an outer noun phrase and a parenthetical, apposition, or coordinated-clause introduces multiple noun-phrase sub-elements attached to that same head-noun. Validate each sub-element independently if each can inherit the same predicate from the outer phrase. Do not multiply links when coordination occurs at predicate level or when the coordinated material is not a noun-phrase candidate.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: "The records are stored in a designated area (a primary unit or a secondary unit)." -> validate one link for each parenthetical noun phrase.
FP: "The records are stored in a designated area or removed later." -> do not validate two links because the coordination is between predicates, not noun phrases.
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: The rule is based on scope and attachment: one predicate can govern several coordinated noun phrases under a shared outer phrase. That validation logic is independent of architecture style because it relies on sentence structure rather than on any particular system vocabulary.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: each style can express alternatives or sub-elements through parenthetical or appositive coordinated noun phrases under one governing predicate. The validation criterion is purely structural—shared predicate scope over multiple noun phrases—so it remains stable across all five. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: Do not approve a candidate from partial-match on a shared head-noun alone. When the document mention is a multi-word-phrase, require either exact-match or compatible modifier, possessive, or qualifier-clause support for the same phrase; if the modifier structure differs, treat the match as unsupported unless another independent cue in the same local context confirms the candidate. Predicate attachment should be checked on the full phrase, not only on the head-noun.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: The introducing-sentence names the exact-match multi-word-phrase "red unit," and the follow-up-sentence repeats "the red unit" with the same predicate.
FP: A sentence contains "blue unit" inside a qualifier-clause, and the linker approves the candidate "red unit" only because both phrases share the head-noun "unit."
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: This rule relies only on surface form, modifier structure, and local predicate attachment. Those cues are discourse-level and do not depend on any particular architecture organization or naming convention.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: in each case, documentation can contain multi-word-phrase mentions with shared head-noun and differing modifiers, so the need to validate modifier and qualifier-clause compatibility remains the same. The rule does not assume any style-specific entity type or relation, only syntactic support. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: Distinguish direct mention from possessive or nested mention. If the predicate is attached to a sub-phrase introduced through possessive, qualifier-clause, or another nested modifier, do not treat the larger phrase as directly supported unless the larger phrase itself is also the predicate-bearing mention. Namespace-prefix or partial-match overlap is not sufficient to upgrade a related structure into a direct mention.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: The sentence states that "silver element" satisfies the predicate, and the exact-match phrase is the subject-position mention.
FP: The sentence states that "silver element's inner phrase" satisfies the predicate, and the linker approves "silver element" even though the predicate is attached to the nested phrase rather than the larger possessive phrase.
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: The distinction between direct mention and nested mention is a general syntactic property. It applies whenever documentation uses possessive or embedded phrases, regardless of how the architecture is organized.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: all five can describe entities through larger phrases and sub-phrases, and predicate attachment can target either level. The rule depends only on possessive and nested phrase structure, not on style-specific semantics. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: Treat a reduced form, short form, or namespace-prefix as alias-defined only when local discourse establishes it. Accept alias-of propagation only if an antecedent exact-match appears in a nearby introducing-sentence, apposition, or alias-defined-parenthetically construction; otherwise keep the reduced form ambiguous. A bare head-noun or shortened multi-word-phrase without such establishment must not seed approval.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: An introducing-sentence presents "long phrase (LP)," and a follow-up-sentence uses "LP" with the same antecedent in local context.
FP: A sentence uses only "phrase" after several candidates with similar head-noun forms have appeared, and the linker treats it as alias-of one specific longer candidate without any apposition, parenthetical, or exact-match establishment.
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: Alias establishment through antecedent, apposition, and parenthetical introduction is a discourse phenomenon independent of architecture style. The rule constrains abbreviation and reduction using local textual evidence only.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: all five styles may use shortened references, but the requirement for local antecedent or parenthetical establishment is unchanged across them. The rule uses only discourse cues and avoids any style-bound assumptions. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: When a multi-word-phrase or exact-match mention appears in subject-position and is immediately followed by a copular predicate, apposition, or clear relational predicate, treat that sentence as positive structural evidence for the subject mention. Accept forms where the predicate assigns identity, responsibility, containment, or cross-reference, even if the mention is not repeated elsewhere in the local window. Do not promote a generic head-noun phrase that appears only in predicate position without a subject-position antecedent.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: "The North Unit is the primary coordination point."
FP: "The primary coordination point is described below."
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: The rule depends only on sentence-position, predicate form, and antecedent anchoring. It does not rely on any domain lexicon or style-specific naming convention, so it applies wherever documentation uses definitional or relational sentences.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: in each case, documentation can introduce an element by placing the mention in subject-position and assigning a predicate with identity or relation information. The cue is syntactic and discourse-based rather than architectural. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: If a sentence introduces a multi-word-phrase and a nearby follow-up-sentence uses a shortened exact-match fragment or head-noun-derived alias in subject-position, propagate the same seed when the local antecedent chain is unique. Give strongest weight to alias-defined-parenthetically, apposition, or immediate reuse after an introducing-sentence. Block propagation when a competing antecedent with the same head-noun is equally near.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: "The Meridian Cluster (Meridian) coordinates requests. Meridian forwards updates to a peer." 
FP: "The Meridian Cluster coordinates requests. The cluster forwards updates to a peer."
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: The rule uses local discourse continuity, abbreviation formation, and antecedent uniqueness rather than any component type. Shortened reuse after introduction is common across documentation styles and naming schemes.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: each style can contain long mentions followed by shortened reuse or parenthetical aliasing. The decision criterion is local alias-of behavior and antecedent competition, not architecture-specific semantics. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: When an introducing-sentence presents a container-of relation by enumerating multiple exact-match or partial-match sub-elements, allow the next follow-up-sentence to inherit the listed item's link if that item reappears in subject-position. Require direct lexical continuity from the list item to the follow-up subject and reject propagation when the follow-up sentence begins with a generic head-noun phrase instead of a listed antecedent.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: "The Atlas group contains Lumen, Orbit, and Vale. Lumen validates incoming records." 
FP: "The Atlas group contains Lumen, Orbit, and Vale. Validation of incoming records is described next."
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: The rule is based on list structure, sentence adjacency, and antecedent reuse. Enumeration followed by focused elaboration is a general documentation pattern independent of implementation style.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: all five can document a larger unit followed by listed sub-elements and then elaborate one item in the next sentence. The trigger is discourse progression from list to follow-up, not style-specific content. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: Reject or down-rank a candidate link when the only trigger is a definite-article plus generic head-noun phrase in predicate, modifier, or object position, and there is no exact-match, namespace-prefix, apposition, alias-defined-parenthetically, or strong antecedent support. Generic descriptive phrases should not be treated as component evidence unless anchored by a nearby subject-position mention or explicit cross-reference. Prefer precision over partial-match when the phrase lacks a recoverable antecedent.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: "The Cedar Unit stores snapshots." 
FP: "The storage path is optimized for snapshots."
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: This rule filters weakly anchored noun phrases using only syntactic position and discourse support. Generic definite-article phrases occur in all forms of technical prose, so the rejection criterion is broadly applicable.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: each style uses generic descriptive phrases in predicates and modifiers, and those phrases are not reliable identifiers without anchoring. The rule constrains overreach using discourse evidence only. Passes.

patterns_proposed.rule_text: When a sentence contains a clear relational predicate that cross-references a second mention, approve the target-side mention as linked evidence in addition to the subject-side mention if the target has exact-match, partial-match with unique antecedent, or alias-of support. Treat the relational predicate as bidirectional evidence only when the target is explicitly realized as a noun phrase in the same clause or coordinated-clause. Do not infer a target from a predicate that names only an activity or quality without an explicit target mention.
patterns_proposed.example_block:
TP: "The Ember Unit forwards updates to the Horizon Module." 
FP: "The Ember Unit improves update handling."
patterns_proposed.why_it_transfers: The rule relies on cross-reference structure between subject and object mentions, not on any particular architecture vocabulary. Explicit relational predicates are a general discourse mechanism for expressing links between documented elements.
patterns_proposed.abstraction_check_cot: Tested against microservice/event-sourced/layered/pipe-filter/hexagonal: all five styles can express relations through subject-to-target predicates with explicit noun-phrase targets. The approval condition is syntactic explicitness plus target anchoring, which is style-invariant. Passes.
